newsitem.title: PERU: Lima shrs off on Wall Street falls, profit-taking.
newsitem.headline: Lima shrs off on Wall Street falls, profit-taking.

text.p: Lima stocks ended lower in thin trading Wednesday on a reaction to falls on Wall Street, profit-taking, and a lack of domestic economic news, brokers said.
They predicted the market would remain stable or continue falling in Thursday's session on the same factors.
"The fall in New York drags the region's bolsas down and, consequently, ours," said Luis Cueva, of Argos brokerage.

"Tomorrow, the market could be stable, or fall slightly on the influence of the Dow Jones index and the lack of (economic) expectations in the local market," said another broker, who asked not to be named.

In Wednesday's session, the General Index .IGRA lost 1.18 percent to 1,437.2 points while the blue-chip Selective Index .ISEL fell 1.47 percent to 2,050.1 points, according to preliminary market figures.
Total market volume was a low 15.9 million soles ($6.1 million) on 1,334 trades.
Among leaders, benchmark Telefonica del Peru lost 2.51 percent to 5.05 soles on 777,299 shares, while miner Minsur SA MINt.LMu slipped 3.68 percent to 9.15 soles on 108,039 shares.

Electricity company Edegel EDE.LM lost 5.34 percent to 1.24 soles on 436,445 shares, while another electricity firm, Luz del Sur, finished off 6.25 percent at 3.15 soles after news that the state was selling its stock in the company at 3.10 soles.
